{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares outcomes in human clinical trials with preclinical dog trials for gene therapy in inherited retinal dystrophies, explicitly stating 'Outcomes in human clinical trials are compared and contrasted with the result of the preclinical dog trials.' This directly addresses the concordance between animal model results and human clinical outcomes for a specific intervention (gene therapy) and indication (inherited retinal dystrophies).",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "The RPE65 gene therapy trials to treat childhood blindness are a good example of how studies in dogs have contributed to therapy development. Outcomes in human clinical trials are compared and contrasted with the result of the preclinical dog trials.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "ophthalmology"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Dog Models for Blinding Inherited Retinal Dystrophies",
  "model_type": "spontaneous-veterinary",
  "model_evidence": "Spontaneous canine models exist for several inherited retinal dystrophies. This review will summarize the models and indicate where they have been used in translational gene therapy trials.",
  "species": [
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Dog Models for Blinding Inherited Retinal Dystrophies",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study mentions improvements in 'retinal function as assessed by the electroretinogram (ERG) and also in vision as assessed by obstacle course vision testing' and 'improved visual function in some of the patients', indicating both functional outcomes and biomarker-like assessments."
}
